_sources.discrepancies: NCSL lists LA as 'photo ID requested' (non-strict). SoS confirms voters without photo ID may sign an affidavit and cast a regular ballot. Louisiana uses a jungle primary (top-two) system, not a party primary runoff. The statewide primary is a nonpartisan jungle primary; runoffs exist but are not party-locked. No party-locked runoff rule applies. [2026-06-10] Rebuilt the 2026 election list from the SoS 2026 Elections Calendar (revised 05/2026): Louisiana's congressional election system changed for 2026. Party primary May 16 (closed: U.S. Senate, Supreme Court, PSC, BESE; reg. deadlines 4/15 in person/mail, 4/25 online; early voting 5/2-5/9); party primary runoff June 27 (reg. 5/27 and 6/6; early voting 6/12-6/20, advanced one day for Juneteenth); November 3 general (U.S. Senate general + OPEN primary for U.S. House per Act 7 of 2026, and open primary for other offices; reg. 10/5 and 10/13; early voting 10/20-10/27); December 12 open general/runoff (reg. 11/12 and 11/21; early voting 11/28-12/5). Previous entries (Oct 10 'jungle primary', Nov 21 'general') did not match the enacted 2026 schedule and were replaced. runoffRules left hasRunoff=false/partyLocked=false: Louisiana's runoffs are not locked to first-round primary participation (closed-primary runoff access follows party registration, which the closed-primary gate covers).

votingRules.expirationRule: Photo ID must not be expired. Louisiana issues free special ID cards for voters who cannot obtain one. Details: https://www.sos.la.gov/ElectionsAndVoting/Vote/GoVotePhotoIDRequirements/Pages/default.aspx
votingRules.impedimentDeclaration: Voters without photo ID may cast a provisional ballot. Alternatively, a poll commissioner who knows the voter may vouch for their identity.
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Louisiana prohibits use of wireless communication devices in the voting booth. You may bring written notes.
additionalRules: Beginning in 2026 (Act 640 of 2024 and Act 1 of the 2024 First Extraordinary Session), U.S. Senate, Louisiana Supreme Court, BESE, and PSC use closed party primaries (May 16, 2026) with a party primary runoff (June 27, 2026); nominees advance to the November 3, 2026 general election.

U.S. House and most state/local offices use Louisiana's open ('jungle') primary on November 3, 2026 (Act 7 of the 2026 Regular Session): all candidates appear on one ballot regardless of party, and if no candidate wins a majority, the top two advance to the December 12, 2026 open general (runoff).

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Starting in 2026, Louisiana uses closed party primaries for U.S. Senate, Supreme Court, BESE, and PSC (Act 1 of the 2024 First Extraordinary Session; Act 640 of 2024): participation in a party's primary (May 16, 2026) and primary runoff (June 27, 2026) is limited by party registration, subject to each party's rules. U.S. House and most other offices still use the open 'jungle' primary on November 3, 2026, where all candidates appear on one ballot and the top two advance to a December 12, 2026 runoff if no one wins a majority.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: A partir de 2026, Luisiana utiliza primarias cerradas de partido para el Senado de los EE. UU., la Corte Suprema, BESE y PSC (Ley 1 de la Primera Sesion Extraordinaria de 2024; Ley 640 de 2024): la participacion en la primaria de un partido (16 de mayo de 2026) y en su segunda vuelta (27 de junio de 2026) esta limitada por el registro de partido, segun las reglas de cada partido. La Camara de Representantes de los EE. UU. y la mayoria de los demas cargos siguen usando la primaria abierta ('jungle') el 3 de noviembre de 2026, donde cada candidato, sin importar su partido, aparece en una sola boleta y los dos primeros avanzan a una segunda vuelta el 12 de diciembre de 2026 si nadie obtiene la mayoria.
